question.worked_solution:
We recognize that the series looks similar to the Maclaurin expansion for $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3!}+\frac{{x}^{5}}{5!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}{x}^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=\frac{5\pi }{6}$ into our Maclaurin expansion gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{5\pi }{6}) & =\frac{5\pi }{6}-\frac{(5\pi /6)^{3}}{3!}+\frac{(5\pi /6)^{5}}{5!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}(5\pi /6)^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}+⋯ \\ \frac{1}{2} & =\frac{5\pi }{6}-\frac{(5\pi /6)^{3}}{3!}+\frac{(5\pi /6)^{5}}{5!}-⋯+\frac{(-1)^{n}(5\pi /6)^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!}+⋯\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the sum of the series is $\frac{1}{2}.$
